editorial:
Imagine meeting a guy who tells you that you are stuck in life and the only way out is to literally put your soul in a box. That is exactly what happens to Bum, a man who is talked into selling his soul to a pawnbroker by a sneaky character named Axel. It sounds totally wild, but the movie plays it out in a way that makes you wonder if it could actually happen. The vibe is a bit strange and old-school since it is a Yugoslavian TV movie, but that just adds to the weirdness of the plot. You will find yourself wondering if Bum is actually changing for the better or if he is just being played for a fool.

What really works here is how the movie handles the weird concept without getting too confusing. The acting is solid, and the slow build-up makes the surprises hit harder. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies, but it is a great pick for a quiet night in. You should definitely try to find a high-quality version, like streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV. If you love owning physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is the way to go for the best picture.
endingExplained: At the end, you see that selling your soul was not the magic fix Bum thought it was. He finds out that without his true self, he is just a shell of a person. The twist is that the pawnbroker and Axel were just using him. Bum eventually realizes he has to get his soul back to be whole again. He learns that your struggles are what make you human, and he finally regains his identity in the closing scenes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange stories about human nature and odd twists.
